# frontend/admin

The management background uses pnpm workspace, organized by "thin host + core base + optional business modules + engineering tools". The host is only responsible for combination and startup; pages, requests, RPC types and business dependencies belong to the corresponding module package.

dependency direction is fixed to `app -> business module -> core`. The core does not depend on any business modules, and business modules do not reference each other by default; when reuse is really needed, they can only use the Interface exposed by the other party's `package.json#exports`.

## Directory Responsibilities

```text
frontend/admin
├── apps/admin                        # 装配当前全部 module 的默认宿主
├── packages/core                     # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-core 底座
│   ├── src/api/{base,system}         # 按 Proto 领域组织的底座请求
│   ├── src/components                # 公共组件
│   ├── src/layouts                   # 布局
│   ├── src/modules                   # 模块注册 interface
│   ├── src/rpc                       # 登录、菜单和底座能力 Proto 类型
│   └── src/views                     # 登录与静态错误页面
├── packages/modules/system           # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-system
│   └── src/{api,rpc,views}           # API 与 RPC 按 Proto 领域层级维护
├── packages/cli                      # @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli
│   └── templates/business-workspace  # 完整 pnpm workspace 模板
├── internal/vite-config              # 当前仓库宿主构建配置
├── internal/tsconfig                 # 共享 TypeScript 配置
├── internal/lint-config              # 共享 Oxlint 配置
├── scripts/build-package.mjs          # core 与业务模块的 npm 发布构建器
├── package.json                       # workspace 命令与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── tsconfig.json                      # workspace TypeScript 路径映射
└── turbo.json
```

`apps/admin/src/module-manifest.ts` is the only source of default host module configuration, and declares the runtime loader, Vite scanning package and pre-built dependencies; `apps/admin/src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules of the current host by default. Core's business view directory only retains the login page. 403, 404, 500, and Pending are provided by core with default static implementations; the personal center, AI assistant, and system management pages are all provided by `systemAdminModule`. The personal center and AI assistant dynamically register routes through the backend menu and do not declare static business routes in the host.

## Root directory file

| path | function |
| -------------------------------------- | ----------------------------------------------------------------- |
| `apps/` | A collection of runnable management hosts; the current default host is `admin`.                  |
| `packages/core/` | Publishable admin runtime, layouts, components and base pages.                      |
| `packages/modules/` | A collection of optional business modules, APIs and pages are maintained together within the module.                    |
| `packages/cli/` | Publishable standalone business workspace command line tool and template.                     |
| `internal/` | Vite, TypeScript and lint configuration packages only for use by the current source code repository.          |
| `scripts/build-package.mjs` | Generate a copy of the npm package source code and TypeScript declaration, and convert the core internal source code alias. |
| `package.json` | Declare workspace-level commands, tool dependencies, Node and pnpm versions.              |
| `pnpm-lock.yaml` | Fixed dependency resolution results for the entire workspace.                               |
| `pnpm-workspace.yaml` | Declare the workspace package under `apps`, `packages`, and `internal`.         |
| `tsconfig.json` | Inherit the shared configuration and declare the source code path mapping of this warehouse.                            |
| `turbo.json` | Defines development, build, release build, and type checking task relationships.                      |
| `AGENTS.md` | Collaboration and code constraints of the management directory.                                      |
| `.editorconfig` | General editor indentation, newline and character set rules.                                |
| `.gitignore` | The management-side local product ignores the rules.                                          |
| `.oxlintignore` | Oxlint scan exclusion rules.                                             |
| `.prettierignore`, `.prettierrc.cjs` | Prettier exclusion range and format configuration.                                     |
| `.stylelintignore`, `.stylelintrc.cjs` | Stylelint exclude scope and style rules.                                    |
| `lint-staged.config.cjs` | Management-side temporary file check configuration used by warehouse-level Git hook.                    |
| `commitlint.config.cjs` | Git submission information verification rules.                                            |
| `postcss.config.cjs` | PostCSS and browser prefix handling configuration.                                    |
| `README.md` | workspace architecture, public commands and module access instructions.                          |

Each subdirectory containing `package.json` has a sibling `README.md`, which describes the package's internal file and directory responsibilities.

The management side publishes `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core`, `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` and
`@liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli`. The default host `@liujitcn/kratos-admin` is a private package and cannot be entered.
npm packaging and distribution manifest.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/admin
pnpm install
pnpm dev
pnpm check:exports
pnpm test
pnpm type:check
pnpm lint:oxlint
pnpm build
pnpm build:package
```

In the `frontend/admin` directory, you can also execute common processes through the upper-level Makefile:

```bash
make -C .. run-admin
make -C .. check-admin
make -C .. build-admin
make -C .. package-admin
```

The default host address is `http://localhost:8848`. The environment variable is located in `apps/admin/.env*`, the development mode API agent and the production build output directory are managed uniformly by the host Vite configuration; the current production build is written to `backend/data/admin`.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by the management side are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The language keys and placeholder sets are verified when registering the module. The login page and the top toolbar share the locale store. Switching languages ​​does not refresh the page, and retains the current routing, query parameters and unsubmitted forms.

The language preference is saved as `kratos-admin:locale`. Axios, refresh token, native fetch, SSE and Swagger requests are uniformly sent to `Accept-Language`; dynamic menus and dictionaries are returned by the backend by locale, and fall back to the main language when the current language translation is missing. To add a new language, you need to synchronize the back-end error directory, the six front-end language package directories of the three workspaces, and code generation `catalog.json`, and then execute `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory; the registration file and Day.js mapping are generated by the script. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

API is organized into directories such as `api/base`, `api/system` according to Proto first-level fields; RPC retains complete Proto levels such as `rpc/base/v1`, `rpc/system/admin/v1`. RPC types are placed according to real consumer ownership: core retains login, menu, user information and service types required during startup capabilities; System self-contained system management, personal center, AI and its dependency types. After modifying Proto, execute `make ts-admin` in `backend`. The command will clean and generate RPCs for core and system according to two Buf configurations respectively; execute `make ts` when you need to generate three front-end RPCs at one time. When the server-side contract has not completed fine-grained splitting, the same generated file may temporarily contain methods that are not called by the current package, and the generated file is not manually written.

The core internal source code uses `@/*`; the business module uses `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core/*` and its own package name. Vue Router is used for page jumps between modules, and cross-directory relative references are prohibited for code reuse.

root TypeScript path and host Vite source code alias only map the entry declared by `package.json#exports` for each npm package. The `@/*` used internally by the core implementation is retained due to source code transfer compilation, but `pnpm check:exports` will scan imports in applications, core, business modules and internal build configurations, and reject undisclosed subpaths, non-core `@/*` references and business module cross-package relative references; warehouse-level pre-commit will first process the temporary files and then execute core Dependency direction and package export bounds checking.

## module interface

core exports `bootstrapAdminApp`, `defineAdminModule`, the view registry, and the top tools, user menu, and routing behavior extensions. The business module entrance declares the name and page loader to access the dynamic page:

```ts
import type { Component } from "vue";
import { defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

const views = import.meta.glob<{ default: Component }>("./views/**/*.vue");

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  views
});
```

business page only registers the module prefix path, so `views/list/index.vue` is uniformly parsed by `order/list/index`, and the `list/index` unprefixed alias is not provided. The `component` of the backend menu must write the complete module path; even if different modules contain `views` pages with the same name, they will not cover each other. The host declares the module in `src/module-manifest.ts`, `src/modules.ts` loads and exports all modules by default, and the Vite build configuration is derived from the manifest:

```ts
export const adminModuleManifest = [
  {
    packageName: "@order/admin-module",
    load: async () => (await import("@order/admin-module")).orderAdminModule
  }
];
```

### Replace static page

core exposes the fixed view keys of all static pages through `ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS`:

| Properties | View Keys |
| -------------- | --------------- |
| `LOGIN` | `login/index` |
| `FORBIDDEN` | `error/403` |
| `NOT_FOUND` | `error/404` |
| `SERVER_ERROR` | `error/500` |
| `PENDING` | `error/pending` |

The business module explicitly maps any of its pages to fixed view keys through `staticViews`, and the later registration module replaces the first registration implementation:

```ts
import { ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS, defineAdminModule } from "@liujitcn/kratos-admin-core";

export const orderAdminModule = defineAdminModule({
  name: "order",
  staticViews: {
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.NOT_FOUND]: () => import("./components/NotFound.vue"),
    [ADMIN_STATIC_VIEWS.PENDING]: () => import("./components/Pending.vue")
  }
});
```

Normal `views` is always isolated by module name, only `staticViews` is replaceable Seam. The npm Interface of core only exposes module access, component whitelist, and stable entrances such as `request`, `navigation`, `table`, `security`, `stores/runtime`; business modules must not rely on the internal source code path of core.

## Create business project

The business project generated by CLI itself is also a pnpm workspace, including an independent host and a publishable business module package:

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-admin-cli create shop-admin --module shop,order

# 当前仓库开发
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop,order
pnpm module:create ../shop-admin --module shop --module order
```

generates results:

```text
shop-admin
├── apps/admin
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/shop
│   └── README.md
├── packages/modules/order
│   └── README.md
├── scripts/build-package.mjs
├── package.json
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml
├── README.md
├── tsconfig.json
└── turbo.json
```

CLI imports `@liujitcn/kratos-admin-system` by default first, and then imports and creates its own module according to the `--module` parameter sequence. `--module` is reusable and also accepts comma-separated names; `--with` only adds additional published modules to the host portfolio, without creating their source code or creating implicit dependencies between business modules. The CLI refuses to overwrite an existing directory.

# frontend/taro-app

`frontend/taro-app` is a standalone pnpm workspace that implements the same application functionality and vision as `frontend/uni-app` in React 18 and Taro 4. Currently supports H5 and WeChat mini programs, including home page, login, agreement, WebView, personal center, settings, personal information and AI assistant, but does not include mall, order, payment or recommendation services.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/taro-app
├── apps/taro-app                 # 私有 Taro 宿主，不发布
├── packages/core                 # 运行时、基础页面和构建 runner
├── packages/ui                   # NutUI 主题与按需图标适配
├── packages/modules/system       # 个人中心、设置、资料和 AI
├── packages/cli                  # 独立 workspace 脚手架
├── scripts                       # package exports 边界检查
├── package.json                  # 公共命令和开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml           # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                    # 跨包任务依赖
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
apps/taro-app -> packages/modules/* -> packages/ui -> packages/core
```

core does not depend on UI or business modules; system only provides reuse capabilities through the core and UI's public exports; the host is only responsible for combining modules and platform configuration.

Detailed description:

- [Private Host](apps/taro-app/README.md)
- [Application Base](packages/core/README.md)
- [UI Basic Package](packages/ui/README.md)
- [system module](packages/modules/system/README.md)
- [Project Scaffolding](packages/cli/README.md)

## Page assembly

`apps/taro-app/src/module-manifest.ts` is a unique module manifest, and the order of declaration determines the override priority for pages, stable `viewKey` and icons. The module declares runtime capabilities through `defineKratosTaroModule()` and exposes the build-time page description through `defineKratosTaroBuildModule()`.

The host only submits fixed `pages/bootstrap` pages. The core runner completes the following operations before development or build begins:

- Scan each module for `src/views/**/*.tsx`, ignoring `components` at any level.
- Generate page wrapper and page config, mount the self-drawn `KratosTabBar` in a unified manner, and complete the top bar consistent with uni-app for the H5 default navigation page.
- Split main package and sub-package by `pages*` root directory.
- Merge each module `src/static` to the host. Priority will be given to existing files on the host, and priority will be given to files with the same name as modules registered.
- Restore the original `app.config.ts` after the build exits and delete the temporary file.

The page wrapper is mounted and self-drawn in a unified manner `KratosTabBar`; the fixed home page and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time, and `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the native effect of WeChat, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab.

exits abnormally, the next command will be automatically restored based on `.kratos-taro-app-pages-state.json`. H5 and WeChat applet development processes can hold the same page assembly transaction at the same time; the runner will only restore the host file after all processes exit. The default product directories for the two targets are `dist/h5` and `dist/mp-weixin` respectively.

## Development and Construction

```bash
cd frontend/taro-app
pnpm install
pnpm dev:h5
pnpm dev:mp-weixin
pnpm build:h5
pnpm build:mp-weixin
```

The upper-level Frontend Makefile provides the corresponding aggregation entry:

```bash
make -C .. run-taro-app      # 微信小程序开发
make -C .. check-taro-app
make -C .. build-taro-app    # H5 构建
make -C .. package-taro-app
```

- The default H5 development address is `http://localhost:5002`, `/api` and `/events` are proxied to `http://localhost:7001`.
- H5 production product is written to `backend/data/taro-app`, and the access address is `/taro-app/`.
- WeChat applet development and production products are written into `apps/taro-app/dist/mp-weixin`, and WeChat developer tools can be directly imported into this directory.
- The environment file is located in the workspace root directory, and the variable name is the same as uni-app Be consistent: `VITE_APP_PORT`, `VITE_APP_BASE_PATH`, `VITE_APP_BASE_API`, `VITE_APP_API_URL`, `VITE_APP_STATIC_API`, `VITE_APP_STATIC_URL`. H5 will overlay `.env.development-h5` or `.env.production-h5` on the base schema file.
- `KRATOS_TARO_OUTPUT_ROOT` is only used to override the build output directory and is not an API environment variable.

Design width is 750. Migrated from uni-app, `rpx` is directly written as Taro design draft `px`; the original physical pixels must be maintained. `px` is not converted when using Taro.

Packaging resources that require fixed paths in the module are placed in `src/static`. Images directly displayed on the page are statically imported through the `static/*` export of the corresponding package, such as `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core/static/images/avatar.png`, ensuring that Webpack generates correct references in H5 and WeChat page chunks; `resolveBundledAsset('static/...')` is only used for runtime paths such as dynamic menu icons that cannot be statically imported.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by Taro are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module; login, home page, status page, WebView, personal center, settings, information and AI pages all use fixed copy through `t(key)`. The language preference is saved as `kratos-app:locale`, and the stable routing and business fields will not be changed after switching.

All `Taro.request`, file uploads, and SSE requests are sent uniformly to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend, and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; adding a new language requires synchronizing the backend error directory, the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces and code generation `catalog.json`, and then executing `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

## RPC generation

Taro RPC templates are unified at `backend/api`:

- `buf.taro-app.typescript.gen.yaml` generates core RPC.
- `buf.taro-app.core.typescript.gen.yaml` Generate system RPCs.

```bash
pnpm generate:rpc
# 等价于
make -C ../../backend ts-taro-app
```

RPC is a generated product and cannot be modified manually.

## CLI

```bash
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create my-app
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create shop-app --module shop,order
pnpm dlx @liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli create my-app --with @acme/customer-module
```

The generated project follows the same React/Taro technology stack, module list, runner transaction protocol and H5/WeChat construction method. The local module independently maintains `pages`, runtime entrance and construction period entrance, which is suitable for subsequent adding capabilities to the mall by business domain.

## Package and verification

The four public package versions must be consistent:

- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-core`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-ui`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-system`
- `@liujitcn/kratos-taro-app-cli`

```bash
pnpm lint
pnpm tsc
pnpm test
pnpm check:exports
pnpm build:packages
pnpm build:h5
pnpm build:mp-weixin
```

`check:exports` validates public targets, version consistency, and cross-package import boundaries; `test` overrides modules covering priorities, navigation, runner transactions, CLI scaffolding, and AI SSE; `build:packages` generates 4 in `dist/npm` tarball.

# frontend/uni-app

`frontend/uni-app` is an independent pnpm workspace that provides directly runnable uni-app host, publishable application base, system business module and project scaffolding. The technology stack is `uni-app + Vue 3 + TypeScript + Vite + Pinia + Sass`, currently supporting H5 and WeChat applets.

The application side only reuses the layering idea of ​​the management side and does not rely on the source code or workspace of `frontend/admin`. Currently, the home page, login, agreement, WebView, personal center, settings, personal information and AI assistant are retained, and the mall, order, payment or recommendation services are not included.

## Workspace

```text
frontend/uni-app
├── apps
│   └── uni-app                # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app，默认宿主，不发布
│       ├── src
│       │   ├── pages/bootstrap
│       │   ├── module-manifest.ts
│       │   ├── manifest.json
│       │   └── pages.json
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── packages
│   ├── core                   # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core v0.0.17
│   │   ├── src                # 底座运行时、页面、状态和构建插件
│   │   ├── test
│   │   ├── README.md
│   │   └── package.json
│   ├── modules
│   │   └── system             # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system v0.0.17
│   │       ├── src            # 个人中心、设置和 AI
│   │       ├── README.md
│   │       └── package.json
│   └── cli                    # @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-cli v0.0.17
│       ├── bin
│       ├── src
│       ├── test
│       ├── README.md
│       └── package.json
├── scripts                    # 包导出边界检查
├── README.md                  # workspace 总览和公共命令
├── package.json               # workspace 脚本与公共开发依赖
├── pnpm-workspace.yaml        # workspace 包范围
└── turbo.json                 # 跨包任务依赖与缓存配置
```

The dependency direction is fixed to:

```text
@liujitcn/kratos-uni-app
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-system
  -> @liujitcn/kratos-uni-app-core
```

- `core` Responsible for authentication, requests, configuration, Pinia, base pages, status pages, dynamic navigation and building plugins.
- `system` is responsible for the personal center, information, settings and AI pages, and only reuses base capabilities through the public exports of `core`.
- `apps/uni-app` only maintains the host entry, manifest, module list, bootstrap page and Vite configuration.
- `cli` creates a separate pnpm workspace with the same structure.

For the directory boundaries, functions and public entries of each package, see:

- [Host Application](apps/uni-app/README.md)
- [Application Base](packages/core/README.md)

## Page assembly

The host maintains a unique module list in `apps/uni-app/src/module-manifest.ts`, and the order determines the static view override priority:

```ts
export const moduleManifest = [coreModule, systemModule]
```

Each module is declared using `defineKratosAppModule()`:

- `pages`: Page styling and optional physical routing overrides.
- `views`: Stable mapping of `viewKey` to physical pages.
- `icons`: In-module icons that can be referenced by dynamic navigation.

The build plug-in automatically scans the `src/views/**/*.vue` of each module and ignores the `components` directory at any level. Post-registration modules can replace the previous module's static pages with the same physical route or `viewKey`.

## Dynamic navigation

The default menu interface is consistent with the management side `base-menu` service:

```text
GET /api/v1/app/base/menu
```

requests the service path to `/v1/app/base/menu`, which is spliced ​​by the unified `/api` base. `base_menu.id = 999` is the hidden fixed root directory of the mobile terminal. The backend queries the enablement page below it layer by layer and maintains a flat response. Core then presses `parent_id` to build the menu tree; you can also access the compatibility contract through `setAppNavigationAdapter()`. The root directory is only associated with mobile menu queries, and each page menu is associated with the protected API actually called by the page.

Menu configuration constraints:

- `path` uses `app/` prefix, supports `:参数` and query.
- `name` Use the `App` prefix.
- The title and main icon use `meta.title`, `meta.icon`, the icon can use an HTTPS address or a key registered in the module `icons`.
- The mobile terminal configuration is placed in `meta.app` without adding independent table fields.
- `meta.app.view_key` must have been registered by the module, and the interface cannot directly deliver any component path.
- `meta.app.access` supports `PUBLIC`, `GUEST_ONLY`, `AUTHENTICATED`, which is semantically consistent with the management-side login permissions.
- The secondary page of the root directory is fixed as a tab. The homepage uses `99901`, mine uses `99909`, and `99902` to `99908` are reserved for business tabs.
- `meta.app.in_tab_bar` of the second-level tab is fixed to true, and the number can only be 0 or 2–5 items; the selected icon uses `meta.app.selected_icon`, and the lower-level page is fixed to non-tab.

The management menu form recursively identifies the entire mobile terminal tree of `999`, displays the logical path, logical name, view key, access mode, mobile terminal icon and API permissions of the page; automatically sets tabs according to the level when submitting, and uniformly packages the mobile terminal configuration into the existing `meta.app`.

Navigation configuration is cached separately in anonymous state and login state. The new configuration will be fully verified and then switched atomically; if the remote end fails, the last successful cache of the current identity will be used; if there is no cache, the local default menu will be used.

## Internationalization

The languages ​​supported by uni-app are automatically discovered by the core and System JSON language packages. The key and placeholder set are verified when registering the module; login, home page, status page, WebView, personal center, settings, information and AI pages all use fixed copy through `t(key)`. The language preference is saved as `kratos-app:locale`, and the stable routing and business fields will not be changed after switching.

All `uni.request`, file uploads, and SSE requests are sent uniformly to `Accept-Language`. The dynamic menu follows the title parsed by the backend, and falls back to the main language when the current language translation is missing; adding a new language requires synchronizing the backend error directory, the six front-end language pack directories of the three workspaces and code generation `catalog.json`, and then executing `make i18n-sync` in the warehouse root directory. For the specific process, see [International Language Expansion Guide](../../docs/国际化语言扩展指南.md).

The page wrapper is mounted and self-drawn in a unified manner `KratosTabBar`; the fixed home page and my page are registered as hidden native tab routes at the same time, and `switchTab` is used when switching to maintain the native effect of WeChat, dynamically expand the tab and then reuse the page stack. Ordinary pages use `navigateTo` first, and subordinate pages will belong along the parent relationship and highlight the corresponding tab. Therefore, the menu level, logical path and `viewKey` can be adjusted after the interface content changes, without having to write each business route in the host.
